sourceAudit.summary: Every source image was reviewed for reusable objects, repeated views, false geometry from mirrors, object pairings, and larger assemblies.

sources.summary: Lower-hall view establishes the chandelier, sloped stair railing, underside wall, ceiling height, and lower purple door relationship.
Close exterior reference for the gold mullions, organic blue trim, stucco reveal, eaves, and adjacent roof plane.
First side of the paneled door with colored glass grid, hardware, jamb, transom, and surrounding wall colors.
Best direct reference for the sculptural painted panel behind the bed; pillows obscure its lower edge.
Shows the monkey lamp and yellow lamp together, with useful scale and shade-profile comparison.
The real bed is on the right. The large left mirror repeats the bed, wall panel, and lamps and must not be interpreted as additional geometry.
Straight-on furniture reference with drawer layout, cabinet door, floral hardware, base plinth, and painted edge trim.
Wide roof-plane view establishes shingle direction, ridge treatment, chimney placement, and one painted chimney face.
Wide garden view establishes the tower proportions, stacked roofs, support posts, decorative panels, plants, and surrounding site context.
Direct pairing of the faceted star mirror and ornate antique lamp; reflections should remain material information, not geometry.
Direct side reference for the rectangular wood shade, stem, base, and adjacent wall-art scale.
Defines the red shelf cubbies and the placed doll, monkey sculpture, pigeon, and colorful house model.
Alternate roof view for shingle reliefs, decorative roof appliques, and chimney-to-roof alignment.
Close front reference for the switch plate, layered pastel backing shapes, and wall mounting depth.
Connects the decorated roof plane to the front window, painted facade, eaves, and chimney edge.
A two-by-two display of four distinct resin plates; each plate is now a separate reusable object while the arrangement remains tracked.

sources.scene: Books and bubble bottle close view
sources.summary: Best material and proportion reference for the stained-glass book stack and green bubble bottle.
Direct lamp profile inside a larger mirror-and-frame wall; the surrounding frames are placement context, not part of the lamp mesh.
Closer complementary view of the tower face panels, layered roof slabs, brackets, posts, garden gate, and nearby plants.
Direct front three-quarter reference for the miniature storefront, striped awning, steps, signs, windows, and planters.
Close view of the house model previously seen in the red shelf, confirming facade relief, roof, windows, door, and side depth.

A multi-object arrangement linking the star mirror, hanging ornament, small chandelier, flower mirror, butterfly, amber vase, and purple dresser; verify the dresser identity before merging with its direct source.
One real green lamp appears beside a mirror reflection; generate one lamp only and use the reflection strictly as a limited alternate view.
Full side view for the upright piano, exposed mechanism, keys, case depth, pedal area, and round stool placement.
Direct three-quarter miniature-house reference with asymmetric volumes, windows, doors, roof peaks, and handmade ceramic surface.
Complementary staircase view establishes the landing, newel post, red handrail, multicolor balusters, dark carpet, and upper door opening.
Master placement reference for three wood window frames, glass shelf tiers, and 34 independent glass vessels.
Second view of the colored door, useful for panel depth, opposite-side trim, jamb proportions, and hardware placement.
Direct front three-quarter reference for the porcelain urn, flower relief, gold handles, lid, stem, and pedestal base.
Direct front view for drawer count, curved legs, lower apron, handles, top depth, and surface wear.
Object cluster links the red lamp, bass guitar, keyboard, and speaker-scale context; each hero object remains a separate model.
Wall-and-table relationship for the painting, black mug, decorative snails, plant, fan, and small colored wall plates.
Primary facade assembly reference showing roof intersections, pastel wall panels, half-timber trim, upper balcony, two canopy types, front door, deck, string lights, and a cluster of plant vessels.
Wide relationship view linking piano, books, bubble bottle, floor lamp, cafe model, ice cream shop, and flower urn across the piano top and shelf.
Straight-on textile reference preserving outline, stitched compartments, hanging rod, corner ties, and material relief.
Wide site assembly showing bridge stairs, rails, repeated but varied lantern posts, potted plants, tree relationship, and garden placements.
Closest alternate chimney face, confirming colored inserts, cap depth, roof pitch, ridge shingles, and eave relationship.

defaultAssetStrategy.summary: Use the white-background inventory image for the first image-to-3D pass, preserve editable material groups, and compare the result against the original source photo.
modelingSteps: Generate the isolated base mesh
Correct silhouette and scale
Separate meaningful material zones
Validate against the source photo

assetStrategies.summary: Use Bed v2 for the clean silhouette, but treat the current source as only one true view. The mirror is false geometry.
modelingSteps: Generate the bed base from Bed v2
Split frame, mattress, pillows, bedding, canopy frame, and drapery into editable submeshes
Add the wall panel as a separate model
Reassemble and validate scale in the room
cautions: Ignore the large mirror copy on the left
Do not fuse the wall panel into the bed mesh

assetStrategies.summary: Combine the close panel view with the wider bed scene to recover full width, relief depth, paint zones, and placement.
modelingSteps: Trace the full panel silhouette
Build shallow relief as separate painted regions
Recover the lower edge behind pillows conservatively
Place behind the bed without merging meshes
captureNeeds: Side raking view for relief depth
cautions: The mirror repeats the panel
The lower panel edge is occluded

assetStrategies.summary: Use the lower-hall and upper-landing photos as complementary views of one staircase, then build the unseen middle flight parametrically.
modelingSteps: Solve floor-to-floor height and stair pitch
Build flight, stringers, treads, risers, and landing
Model newel posts, red rail, and multicolor balusters as separate parts
Add carpet runner and surrounding openings
Place chandelier only after architectural scale is locked
captureNeeds: Full side elevation of the flight
View from the bottom step upward
cautions: Current sources do not show the complete middle flight
Do not infer stair geometry from the railing alone

assetStrategies.summary: Model the window as a reusable facade module with separate glass, gold mullions, blue organic trim, and wall reveal.
modelingSteps: Build the rectangular opening and reveal
Model frame, mullions, and organic trim separately
Use thin glass planes with traced artwork
Instance the module only where proportions match
cautions: Roof planes occlude the lower corners

assetStrategies.summary: Combine the six exterior references and three isolated studies to reconstruct the house roof as one reusable assembly, separate from the chimney and facade.
modelingSteps: Solve the broad front plane and intersecting gable volumes from the source photos
Build ridges, valleys, eaves, fascia, and underside thickness as editable roof modules
Recreate the irregular curving shingle courses and colored roof appliques
Keep the chimney penetration and every facade or canopy element separate
Validate the roof footprint against the overhead and opposite-angle studies
cautions: The generated white-background angles are reconstruction studies, not measured photogrammetry
Do not fuse the chimney, walls, window trim, or entrance canopies into the roof mesh

assetStrategies.summary: Use all four roof photos to reconstruct the chimney's different painted faces and its exact penetration through the roof.
modelingSteps: Align the views around one chimney volume
Model cap, side projections, and colored face inserts
Match roof pitch and flashing interface
Place only after the roof blockout is stable
cautions: Some roof decorations can be mistaken for chimney details

assetStrategies.summary: Treat the turquoise triangular canopy and the smaller brown side canopy as separate facade modules, not one fused entrance object.
modelingSteps: Block the door openings
Model each canopy roof, brackets, and trim separately
Add scalloped doorframe trim and curtain door as separate parts
Place modules against the facade blockout
cautions: The source contains two distinct canopy designs

assetStrategies.summary: Use the white-background grouping as a source-faithful placement guide for the complete courtyard plant-and-vessel arrangement.
modelingSteps: Split every planted specimen and decorative vessel into independently placeable objects
Separate every pot, trunk, branch mass, foliage mass, and sphere into editable geometry
Preserve the agave silhouette, twisted woody branches, sparse conifer, and trailing succulent shapes
Rebuild the loose source-relative placement in the House Exterior assembly
captureNeeds: Rear view of each planted container and vessel
cautions: Only one front view is available
The white urn, black ribbed vessel, and speckled sphere-topped urn are retained for placement but should remain separate from plant geometry

assetStrategies.summary: Use the two source views as opposite-side references for one colored interior door and its frame.
modelingSteps: Align both door elevations
Build slab, colored glass grid, lower panel, jamb, and transom separately
Place side-specific hardware
Verify swing direction before scene placement
cautions: Do not confuse this interior door with the exterior curtain door

assetStrategies.summary: Combine the wide and close garden references to recover the tower's stacked roofs, patterned faces, support posts, and site position.
modelingSteps: Block the central tower volume
Build repeated roof slabs and brackets
Model patterned face panels as modular inserts
Add support posts and bulbs
Place garden and gate context separately
cautions: Foliage hides parts of the base

assetStrategies.summary: Use the close view for glass and lead detail and the wide studio view for stack order, scale, and placement.
modelingSteps: Split the stack into individual book volumes
Model leaded edges and translucent glass panels
Preserve the irregular stack offsets
Reassemble on the piano top
cautions: The wide view is useful for placement, not fine geometry

assetStrategies.summary: Pair the close material reference with the wide placement view; model the bottle independently from the books.
modelingSteps: Build the rectangular translucent bottle
Separate cap and wand
Use the embossed source lettering as texture or shallow relief
Place beside the book stack

assetStrategies.summary: The side source gives overall depth and stool relation; the studio source gives a clear open-front mechanism elevation.
modelingSteps: Block the upright case and key bed
Model exposed action as instanced repeating parts
Separate pedals, lid, fallboard, and panels
Validate depth against the side view
Place tabletop props after the piano scale is final
cautions: Do not fuse the display objects on top into the piano mesh

assetStrategies.summary: Use the shelf view for placement and the close view for the miniature facade, roof, and side depth.
modelingSteps: Generate the house as an independent miniature
Correct facade relief and roof depth from the close view
Keep base and side pieces editable
Place back in the red shelf cubby

assetStrategies.summary: Generate one real lamp; use the mirror copy only as limited material and backside evidence.
modelingSteps: Isolate the real lamp
Model base, stem, socket, and shade separately
Compare the mirror only for visible reverse details
cautions: Do not create two lamps
Do not bridge the real lamp and reflection into one mesh

assetStrategies.summary: Model the bridge and each lantern-post design separately, then place repeated instances according to the garden reference.
modelingSteps: Build bridge steps, deck, rails, and posts as editable modules
Split the visible lantern types
Instance lanterns without erasing design variations
Add plant pots and site placements after structure
captureNeeds: Close views of each lantern type
cautions: The lanterns are related but not identical

assetStrategies.summary: Use the display image only to rebuild placement. Do not ask the generator for one fused window-and-glass mesh.
modelingSteps: Model three wood frames
Model shelf panes and supports
Generate all vessels individually
Place vessels from the window, level, and order map
Validate the full silhouette against the master source
cautions: Exterior garden scenery is not part of the assembly
Reflections are material cues, not duplicate vessels

assetStrategies.summary: Each of the 34 vessels has its own white-background asset and should be generated, corrected, and versioned independently.
modelingSteps: Generate one watertight vessel
Correct rim, stem, base, stopper, and profile
Assign transparent colored glass material
Place from the assembly map
captureNeeds: Optional turntable photos for hero vessels
cautions: Shelf occlusion may require conservative reconstruction
Keep similarly colored vessels as distinct assets

assetStrategies.summary: The four resin plates are separate hero objects with individual relief and color, plus a tracked two-by-two wall arrangement.
modelingSteps: Generate each plate separately
Preserve rim depth and botanical relief
Keep mounting hardware optional
Rebuild the two-by-two wall arrangement
cautions: Do not merge four plates into one texture plane

assemblies.name: Bed Setup
assemblies.intent: Build a high-detail bedroom hero assembly from independently editable bed, panel, lighting, fabric, and room parts.
relations: Wall panel is centered behind the real bed
Canopy fabric spans above the bed but should remain cloth geometry
The left mirror repeats the setup and is not another bed

assemblies.name: Staircase
assemblies.intent: Combine two partial architectural views into one editable flight, landing, railing, carpet, and hallway assembly.
relations: Lower source fixes chandelier and underside placement
Upper source fixes landing, newel, rail, baluster, and carpet design
The unseen middle should be solved from consistent stair pitch rather than invented freeform

assemblies.name: House Exterior
assemblies.intent: Assemble the exterior from reusable architectural modules and scene-specific trim instead of generating one low-resolution house mesh.
plannedParts: Lower curtain door and scalloped frame
relations: The three isolated roof studies clarify the roof planes while the exterior photos remain the source of truth
Roof photos provide complementary chimney faces, roof pitch, and chimney placement
The facade photo anchors balcony, doors, canopies, wall colors, and the Outdoor Plants grouping
Outdoor Plants preserves the courtyard placement while each potted specimen remains independently modelable
The window close view provides reusable trim and glass detail
Garden tower and bridge remain neighboring site assemblies, not house geometry

assemblies.name: Glass Window Display
assemblies.intent: Rebuild all three framed windows, shelf tiers, and 34 independently modeled glass vessels with repeatable placement metadata.
plannedParts: Left, center, and right wood frames
relations: The full display record is a placement guide, not a fused object
Window and level identify the primary placement zone; order runs left to right
Exterior plants and garden views are background only

assemblies.name: Wall Plate Collection
assemblies.intent: Preserve four independent relief plates and their original two-by-two display relationship.
relations: Each plate has unique relief and color
Keep the group arrangement as scene metadata only

assemblies.name: Interior Door
assemblies.intent: Reconcile two sides of one colored-glass door into an operable slab, jamb, transom, and hardware assembly.
relations: Sources show complementary sides
Preserve swing direction and side-specific hardware

assemblies.name: Garden Tower
assemblies.intent: Use two exterior views to reconstruct the tower as an independent garden landmark plus nearby gate and plant context.
relations: Wide view gives site scale
Close view gives face and roof detail

assemblies.name: Red Shelf Display
assemblies.intent: Preserve both reusable shelf contents and their cubby placements.
relations: Colorful house close view improves the object without changing shelf placement
All contents stay as separate assets

assemblies.name: Wall Gallery
assemblies.intent: Track the dresser, mirrors, lighting, hanging ornaments, and tabletop decor as independent assets with one arrangement guide.
relations: Star mirror has a direct close source
Verify whether the dresser in the gallery is the same physical dresser as the direct purple dresser before combining sources

assemblies.name: Piano and Studio Display
assemblies.intent: Recreate the piano, props, and narrow display shelf while keeping every miniature and tabletop object reusable.
relations: Close sources improve individual objects
Wide source fixes piano-top and shelf placement
Props must not be fused into the piano or shelf

assemblies.name: Instrument Corner
assemblies.intent: Keep the lamp, bass, and keyboard as separate assets while preserving their clustered scale relationship.
relations: The image is useful for relative scale but only partial for the instruments

assemblies.name: Wall Art Vignette
assemblies.intent: Preserve the painting, black mug, and snails as separate assets within a small wall-and-table relationship.
relations: Secondary plant and fan are context until cleaner references exist

assemblies.name: Garden Bridge
assemblies.intent: Rebuild the bridge, varied lantern posts, plants, and tree relationship as modular site geometry.
relations: Lanterns repeat by role but differ in shape and color
Plants and pots should remain separately placeable
